steps.title: Identify SNPs and design primers
steps.instruction: Select suitable single‑nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the gene(s) of interest, then design the required primers: Delta Gene forward and reverse primers for pre‑amplification and gene‑expression analysis (provided as an equimolar pool at 100 µM), and SNP‑Type primers consisting of a specific target amplification (STA) primer, a locus‑specific primer (LSP) and two allele‑specific primers (ASP1 and ASP2). Resuspend LSP and STA primers at 100 µM; ASP1 and ASP2 carry proprietary tags and must be ordered from the specified vendor. Record the major‑allele‑specific ASP1 (detected with a FAM‑labelled probe) and the minor‑allele‑specific ASP2 (detected with a HEX‑labelled probe).

steps.title: Order and resuspend primers
steps.instruction: Order any Delta Gene primers that are not supplied in the equimolar pool (e.g., the reverse Delta Gene primer needed for pre‑amplification of the TLR7 rs3853839 region) from a different primer‑production company. Upon receipt, resuspend each primer at a concentration of 100 µM in nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Create primer pool and aliquot
steps.instruction: Combine up to 200 primer pairs for the assay: thaw all primers on ice, vortex and spin briefly, then mix 1 µL of each primer into a fresh tube. Add C1 Dilution Reagent (Fluidigm) to bring the total volume to 200 µL, yielding an equimolar primer pool at 100 µM. Aliquot the pool into single‑use 8 µL tubes to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles and store at –20 °C in the dark; aliquots remain stable for up to 1 year. For gene‑expression‑only targets (e.g., reference gene B2M) also add the corresponding Delta Gene primers to the pool.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from donors
steps.instruction: Using the Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit, isolate gDNA from each donor (up to 10 donors). Acceptable starting material: 3–5 × 10⁶ freshly isolated PBMCs, 3–5 × 10⁶ PBMCs frozen as a pellet at –80 °C, or 3 mL EDTA‑blood frozen at –80 °C. If using EDTA blood, lyse erythrocytes with 3 mL ACK lysis buffer for 3 min, then wash the pellet with PBS for 7 min at 500 g; repeat washes until the pellet is no longer red. Follow the kit protocol, eluting gDNA into two separate Eppendorf tubes with 35–50 µL AE buffer each. Measure DNA concentration with a NanoDrop and retain only samples with >100 ng/µL for downstream steps. (Extraction of up to 10 donors takes ≈60 min.)

steps.title: Perform specific target amplification (STA)
steps.instruction: Use at least 100 ng/µL gDNA as input for the STA reaction. Set up the STA according to the Fluidigm SNP Genotyping User Guide (PN 68000098 Rev. 18, p. 131ff), employing the LSP and STA primers. If no splicing site surrounds the SNP, the same primer set can be used later for mRNA analysis.

steps.title: Set up SNP typing on IFC
steps.instruction: Choose the appropriate Fluidigm Integrated Fluidic Circuit (IFC): the 48.48 IFC (48 SNPs × 48 gDNAs) or the 192.24 IFC (24 SNPs × 192 gDNAs). Follow the corresponding Quick Reference Guide (PN 100‑3910 C1 for 48.48; PN 100‑3913 C1 for 192.24) and the Genotyping with IFC Using SNP Type Assays protocol. Load the STA‑amplified gDNA, the SNP‑Type assay mix (containing LSP, STA, ASP1, ASP2 and the FAM/HEX probes), and the appropriate loading reagents as described in the guides.

steps.title: Aliquot Single Cell‑to‑CT qRT‑PCR reagents
steps.instruction:
Prepare single‑use aliquots of the Thermo Fisher Single Cell‑to‑CT qRT‑PCR Kit in 0.5 mL tubes to avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles. Thaw all reagents on ice, aliquot, then refreeze immediately. Store the Single Cell Lysis Solution at 4 °C; all other reagents have a shelf‑life of ~9 months after receipt. Recommended aliquot volumes (including a small overage) are:
- Single Cell Stop Solution: 2.5 µL per tube (prepare 18 tubes, overage 0.56 µL).
- Single Cell Pre‑Amp Mix: 12.0 µL per tube (prepare 18 tubes, overage 2.02 µL).
- Single Cell SuperScript RT: 3.6 µL per tube (prepare 18 tubes, overage 0.38 µL).
- Single Cell VILO RT Mix: 5.0 µL per tube (prepare 18 tubes, overage 1.16 µL).
- Single Cell DNase I: 1.4 µL per tube (prepare 18 tubes, overage 0.11 µL).
- Single Cell Lysis Solution: 12.0 µL per tube (prepare 189 tubes, overage 2.25 µL).
Note: The Single Cell Pre‑Amp Mix is viscous; pipette carefully.

steps.title: Aliquot C1 Dilution Reagent and Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Divide the Fluidigm C1 Dilution Reagent into 2.8 mL aliquots (or two 1.4 mL aliquots when using 1.5 mL tubes). Aliquot the Fluidigm Cell Wash Buffer into 100 µL portions. Store aliquots at 4 °C to minimise thaw time and prevent cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Aliquot ROX Reference Dye
steps.instruction: Dispense the Thermo Fisher ROX Reference Dye into single‑use 8 µL aliquots. Because the dye is light‑sensitive, keep aliquots in the dark at –20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Prepare FACS Buffer (PBS + 2% FBS)
steps.instruction: Make a fluorescence‑activated cell sorting (FACS) buffer by adding 2 % (v/v) fetal bovine serum (FBS) to phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS). Keep the buffer on ice until use.

steps.title: Combine outermost SNP and Delta primers
steps.instruction: For the pre‑amplification step, mix the outermost primer pair consisting of the SNP‑Type STA primer and the Delta Gene reverse primer (ordered separately if not in the pooled kit). This pair generates the amplicon that will later be analysed separately with the Delta Gene primers (gene‑expression) and the SNP‑Type primers (allele‑specific detection).

description: This protocol describes the specific steps to investigate escape of X-chromosomal genes from X chromosome inactivation (XCI) in human plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs), with the example of TLR7 and CYBB. This protocol can be adapted to investigate the escape of different genes in other cell types. We have also investigated the escape of RPS6KA3, BTK and IL13RA1 from XCI in human pDCs (Hagen et al., 2020). For X chromosomal genes it is also possible to compare the effect of the minor allele in comparison to the major allele at the single-cell level, for example whether the single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) has an influence on the mRNA transcription level. The vast majority of autosomal genes however are expressed in a biallelic fashion. Thus this approach is only feasible for allosomal genes and the roughly 5% of autosomal genes that are randomly expressed in a monoallelic fashion (Gimelbrant et al., 2007). The first step is to identify adequate SNPs in the gene(s) of interest and to design the specific primers, before SNP typing the cohort of interest to identify female individuals with a suitable SNP profile. For this experimental approach there are multiple primers employed. The Delta Gene forward and reverse primers are used for preamplification and gene expression analysis. The Delta Gene primers are primers without any modification and the Delta Gene forward and reverse primers are provided as equimolarly pooled at 100 μM. The SNP Type primers consist of the specific target amplification (STA) primer, the Locus-specific primer (LSP) and the Allele-specific primer (ASP)1 and ASP2. The LSP and STA primer are primers without any modifications. They are individually resuspended at 100 μM. ASP1 and ASP2 are the only primers with specific modifications, hence they cannot be ordered through a different company.
